subject: Post-call: Novafin residency constraints + hosted fallback options
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ingrid Svensson <ingrid.svensson@novafin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Novafin residency constraints + hosted fallback options

Hi Ingrid —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and so Ben/Vivek have the constraints top of mind: 

- Primary requirement: EU-only residency for PII and model context (customer messages, payment metadata).
- User footprint: Majority EU; a smaller APAC user base (Malaysia + Singapore) that cannot send regulated PII to EU by policy — they asked about local routing.
- Preferred path: Novafin would like to start with the fastest path that preserves EU residency. Your TPM mentioned a preference for "hosted" if we can ensure EU-only processing; otherwise dedicated or VPC is acceptable.
- Timeline: Decision target end of October; pilot within Q4 preferred.

Attachments: I’ve attached our concise hosting options summary and the requirements sheet you shared during the call (renamed for this thread).

Immediate next steps I propose: 
1) Ben to confirm which hosted endpoints can be EU-restricted (and whether APAC-origin users can be routed to APAC with non-PII fallback).
2) Vivek to outline Dedicated vs Private VPC lead times and high-level security controls (KMS/HSM, VPC peering, audit logs).
3) Novafin to share any additional compliance docs or tour of your network gating we should know before a pilot.

Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up Wednesday (Oct 6) for a short technical sync? I’ll include solutions engineering.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0147

Attachments referenced: redwood-hosting-options-summary.pdf, novafin-residency-requirements.xlsx

From: Ingrid Svensson <ingrid.svensson@novafin.com>

Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Novafin residency constraints + hosted fallback options

Thanks Lauren — useful recap. A couple clarifications from my side: 

- EU residency requirement is non-negotiable for PII and transaction context. Non-PII telemetry may be less restricted.
- For APAC users: policy team would prefer APAC-local processing where possible; otherwise we need a guarantee that only anonymized or redacted payloads cross borders.
- Security ask: what are your default encryption-at-rest options and KMS integration (we use Azure Key Vault)? Also need estimated SLA for a pilot and production.

I’ve attached the internal residency/processing policy (see Novafin-Residency-Reqs tab). If you can confirm hosting options that satisfy the EU residency constraint we’ll route the pilot approval internally.

—Ingrid
Ingrid Svensson
Product & Compliance Lead, Novafin
ingrid.svensson@novafin.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ingrid Svensson <ingrid.svensson@novafin.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Novafin residency constraints + hosted fallback options

Hi Ingrid — quick technical summary to address the asks from the call: 

1) Hosted API (fastest onramp):
   - We can provision EU-only hosted endpoints that physically process and store data in our eu-west-1 region. This satisfies the PII residency requirement for data at rest and in processing.
   - Caveat: APAC-origin traffic routed into EU still implies cross-border transfer. For APAC users we can either: 
      a) Route to an APAC endpoint (if you want APAC processing) — but for this to be EU-only you would need per-region control on the client side; or
      b) Use client-side redaction/partial anonymization for APAC-origin requests so sensitive fields never leave APAC.

2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs in EU):
   - Can be provisioned in an EU-only environment, with reserved pools, private networking (VPC peering), and HSM/KMS integration. Provides stronger tenancy and simpler billing visibility.
   - Lead time: ~4–6 weeks after contract and infra approval for baseline config; shorter for existing enterprise customers.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem):
   - Full control — deployable into your VPC or on-prem. Longest lead time (6–12+ weeks depending on network approvals).

Security & SLA notes:
- We support Azure Key Vault and customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private; hosted EU endpoints use our EU KMS by default but can integrate with customer KMS on Dedicated.
- SOC2 Type II report and pen-test summary are available — I’ll attach links and can share the full artifacts via secure transfer.

Next steps I recommend:
- Short technical workshop (Solutions Eng + Novafin infra/security) to confirm whether APAC users should be routed to APAC endpoints or use a redaction pattern.
- If Novafin wants EU-only processing for everything, Dedicated or Private VPC is the safer long-term answer. Hosted can meet residency for EU-origin requests with the caveat above.

I’ve pasted a short link with the hosting comparison and included a stub of SLA bullets in the attached doc.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
